evidence.source_sentence: The structure of the polymers was identified by IR and NMR spectroscopy. Specifically, the IR spectra of the poly(ether imide)s revealed that the characteristic bands around 1 768 and 1 716 cm⁻¹ are commonly attributed to the asymmetric and symmetric stretches of carbonyl group of imides, respectively. The C–N band at 1369 cm⁻¹ verified the formation of the imide structure. The NMR data of the polymer PI-1 are listed in the experimental section, and the resonance peaks at 168.0 and 167.9 ppm are ascribed to the carbon of the imide group.

evidence.source_sentence: The elemental analysis data of these polyimides as listed in Table 1 are generally in good agreement with the respective structures for hydrogen, carbon, and nitrogen.
Preparation ofPoly(ether imide)s

The poly(ether imide)s were prepared by the conventional two-step polymerization method, as shown in Scheme 2, which involves ring-opening polyaddition of bis(ether anhydride) BDPCD with diamines DA-1 to DA-7 forming poly(ether amic acid) precursors PAA-1 to PAA-7 and subsequent chemical cyclodehydration.
The poly(ether amic acid)s (PAA-1 to PAA-7) were prepared by gradually adding the bis(ether anhydride) BDPCD to the diamines (DA-1 to DA-7) in DMAc solution.
The obtained viscous poly(ether amic acid) solution was then supplemented by dehydrating agents, such as a mixture of acetic anhydride and pyridine to yield poly(ether imide)s PI-1 to PI-7.
The elemental analysis data of these polyimides as listed in Table 1 are generally in good agreement with the respective structures for hydrogen, carbon, and nitrogen.
